title: Your Business Model Through the Supervisor's Lens
summary: A one-day workshop helping boards and senior managers analyse their business model and strategy the way a supervisor does, and present it with confidence.
intro: This training programme equips boards and senior managers to analyse their own business model and strategy the way a risk-based supervisor does, and to explain its viability and sustainability with confidence and evidence.

sections.Aim and Purpose: To give boards and senior managers the analytical tools supervisors use to judge whether a business model is viable today and sustainable over the plan period, applied to their own firm. Participants leave able to identify their key vulnerabilities before the supervisor does, test their plans and assumptions, and present a credible account of the business model in supervisory engagement.
sections.What It Covers: Why supervisors analyse business models, reading the numbers, concentrations and dependencies, the business environment and competitive position, strategy, projections and stress testing, and presenting the business model to the supervisor.
Intended Audience: Board members, chief executives and senior managers responsible for strategy and the business plan
Finance, risk and compliance staff who prepare business plans, projections and regulatory submissions
Senior managers preparing for a supervisory risk assessment or business model review
Learning Objectives: Explain why and how risk-based supervisors analyse business models and strategy
Interpret the firm's financial performance, capital and key ratios as a supervisor would
Identify concentrations and dependencies that could break the business model
Assess the firm's competitive position and the external environment using structured frameworks
Challenge projections and assumptions using plan-versus-outturn, scenarios and reverse stress tests
Present a clear, evidenced account of the business model and its key vulnerabilities to the supervisor
sections.Structure and Format: Six modules of about one hour each, delivered as a one-day workshop in person, virtually or in a hybrid format. Each module combines a short briefing with a worked case study and an exercise applied to the participants' own firms. It can be delivered on its own or with the companion workshops on governance and supervisory interviews and on supervisory findings and remediation.
sections.Useful Prior Knowledge and Experience: Some familiarity with the firm's business plan and financial statements is helpful. No accounting qualification is required.
Core Reading: IMF, Good Supervision: Lessons from the Field (Working Paper WP/23/181, 2023)
FSB, Principles for an Effective Risk Appetite Framework (2013)
IOSCO, Objectives and Principles of Securities Regulation (2017)

modules.title: Why Supervisors Analyse Business Models
modules.summary: How strategy and business model risk fit into risk-based supervision, what supervisors want to learn and how their conclusions shape the firm's supervisory engagement.
objectives: Explain the link between business model weakness and other risks
Describe what a supervisory business model review covers
Anticipate the questions supervisors will ask about the firm's strategy
syllabus: Strategy, business model and the value chain
Viability now and sustainability over the plan period
Proportionality: what prompts a deeper review
How business model findings feed risk ratings and remediation

modules.title: Reading the Numbers
modules.summary: The quantitative picture supervisors build from the profit and loss account, balance sheet and key risk indicators, and what the trends reveal about how the firm makes money.
objectives: Interpret profitability, cash and capital trends
Break returns down into their drivers
Spot the numbers that will prompt supervisory questions
syllabus: Profit and loss: revenue mix, margins and cost base
Balance sheet: funding, capital quality and tangible net worth
Key ratios, driver trees and sector metrics
Worked example: growing, but who benefits?

modules.title: Concentrations and Dependencies
modules.summary: How concentrations in clients, products, distributors and counterparties, and dependence on outsourced providers and technology, can break a business model.
objectives: Identify critical internal and external dependencies
Test what happens when a dependency fails
syllabus: Client, product, distribution and counterparty concentrations
Hidden shared dependencies across concentrations
Outsourcing, technology and cyber as strategic dependencies
Linking concentrations to risk appetite

modules.title: The Business Environment and Competitive Position
modules.summary: How supervisors assess the macro and competitive environment, and how the firm can evidence a real and durable competitive advantage.
objectives: Apply PESTEL and five forces analysis to the firm
Assess whether the organisation can deliver the strategy
syllabus: PESTEL: which factors matter most for this firm
Five forces, substitution and new entrants
Portfolio choices and where the cash comes from
Testing competitive advantage and organisational alignment

modules.title: Strategy, Projections and Stress Testing
modules.summary: How to make the business plan credible: challenging assumptions, learning from plan versus outturn and using scenarios and reverse stress tests to find what breaks the model.
objectives: Challenge the key assumptions behind projections
Use the firm's forecasting record to build credibility
Design scenarios and reverse stress tests for the business model
syllabus: Why strategies fail: poor design versus poor execution
Assumptions, sensitivities and plan versus outturn
Scenario analysis and reverse stress testing
Execution risk and capability to deliver

modules.title: Presenting Your Business Model to the Supervisor
modules.summary: Bringing the analysis together into an honest statement of key vulnerabilities and mitigants, and presenting it effectively in supervisory meetings and submissions.
objectives: Summarise the firm's key vulnerabilities and mitigants
Prepare the board and management for business model discussions
syllabus: From analysis to key vulnerabilities
What a credible business model narrative looks like
Preparing for supervisory meetings on strategy
Workshop: a business model self-assessment on your own firm

related.title: Engaging Effectively with Your Supervisor: How Firms Are Assessed
related.summary: A ten-module programme showing firms how supervisors assess business models, governance and risk, so they can see themselves as the supervisor does and engage with confidence.

related.title: Fit and Proper for Firms: Appointing and Assessing Key Function Holders
related.summary: A nine-module programme showing firms how to appoint and assess key function holders, prepare applications and interviews, and manage fitness and certification on an ongoing basis.

related.title: Governance Reviews and Supervisory Interviews: Preparing Your Board and Management
related.summary: A one-day workshop on how supervisors assess governance and interview directors and staff, and how licensees can evidence effective governance and prepare openly.

related.title: Recovery and Wind-Down Planning for Firms
related.summary: An eight-module programme helping firms build credible recovery and wind-down plans, from scenarios and triggers to client asset return, testing and supervisory review.

related.title: Regulatory Investigations and Enforcement: Responding as a Firm
related.summary: A ten-module programme showing firms how to prepare for, manage and respond to supervisory investigations and enforcement, from first information request to settlement.

related.title: Regulatory Readiness: Authorisation and Supervisory Engagement
related.summary: A ten-module programme taking firms from licence application through to established supervision, showing how authorities assess applications and supervise new firms.
